articleTitle: Design and Qualification of a High-Speed Low-Power Comparator in 40 nm CMOS Technology
abstract: This paper presents the design methodology, test setup and experimental qualification results of a high-speed low-power threshold comparator in 40 nm CMOS technology intended for the registry of particles landing on a PIN-detector surface in particle detector readout electronics. The operation of the designed comparator is experimentally qualified for ideal digital pulses and analog signals generated by the preceding stages in a targeted potential application.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of Nested Interruptions and Levels of Cognitive Demand on Mental States
abstract: Interruptions to secondary tasks increase cognitive load and emotion. Interruptions force workers to switch jobs. In the two studies, some of these secondary tasks get interrupted, resulting in multiple tasks that must be resumed, known as nested interruptions. We hypothesize that nested interruption and mental task levels increase the mental load and negative emotions and degrade performance. The participant would have to encode the resumption goals for both the primary and the interrupted secondary tasks in working memory. Initially, a preliminary laboratory experiment was conducted on two participants using Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in which one participant had to complete the three tasks (without and with time press and cognitive demand) without interruption, and the other had to complete the tasks with two kinds of interruption (single and nested interruption). Our research can help managers and staff members manage nested interruptions and workloads better.

articleTitle: Monocular Depth Estimation for Autonomous UAV Navigation Based on Deep Learning
abstract: This study focuses on the autonomous navigation and mapping of indoor environments using a drone equipped only with a monocular camera and height measurement sensors. A visual SLAM algorithm was employed to generate a preliminary map of the environment and to determine the drone's position within the map. A deep neural network was utilized to generate a depth image from the monocular camera's input, which was subsequently transformed into a point cloud to be projected into the map. By aligning the depth point cloud with the map, 3D occupancy grid maps were constructed by using ray tracing techniques to get a precise depiction of obstacles and the surroundings. Due to the absence of IMU data from the low-cost drone for the SLAM algorithm, the created maps are inherently unscaled. However, preliminary tests with relative navigation in unscaled maps have revealed potential accuracy issues, which can only be overcome by incorporating additional information from the given sensors for scale estimation.

articleTitle: Modeling, Simulation and Implementation of pi/4-DQPSK modem on SDR
abstract: Article addresses modeling, simulation and implementation of digital modulator/demodulator (modem) with pi/4 differential quadrature phase shift modulation (pi/4-DQPSK) on software-defined radio (SDR) platform. A model of the system was created in GNU Radio Framework. Experimental results of bit error rate (BER) in presence of additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) is obtained through simulation. An experimental RF DQPSK modem was implemented with USRP frontend.

articleTitle: Validation of Buck DC/DC converter inductor influence via experimental evaluation module
abstract: The following work introduces a practical look at a DC/DC Buck converter with the task to verify its use in an industrial application. The principle on which the DC/DC Buck converter works is by using a semiconductor switch, filter group composed of inductor-capacitor, and a diode to step down the voltage at the output of the circuit. The amount of voltage at the output of the circuit depends on the duty cycle "D" on the input of the circuit. When the circuit is operating in continuous conduction mode the duty cycle gives the voltage ratio between the output and input supply. The study is carried out by using an electronic evaluation module with interchangeable components needed to design the converter. The interchangeability of the components allows one to see the different effects and their values have on the overall design. This in turn allows evaluating and choosing the right component for a certain task.

articleTitle: Examination of LLC based DC/DC Resonant Converter at Different Modes of Operation
abstract: This paper presents an examination of a half bridge resonant DC/DC converter based on LLC topology with GaN power transistors. Using GaN transistors allows increasing the switching frequency and thus reducing the size of the transformer as well as reducing the size of the output filter. LTspice simulation results are presented. The experimental setup uses evaluation boards GSP665HPMB-EVBIMS2 and GSP66508HB-EVBIMS2 from "GaN Systems". The switching frequency is up to 1MHz. Experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: An Elementary Emulator Based on Speech-To-Text and Text-to-Speech Technologies for Educational Purposes
abstract: The article examines two innovative technologies Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Speech-to-Text (STT). They have been used to create a tool to facilitate the preparation of learning documentation in English, such as: lectures, laboratory exercises, course projects, tests. The article provides a brief description of TTS and STT technologies; analysis of existing developments; presentation of development trends, synthesizer technologies; a comparison of acoustic and language modeling; description of models that use STT technology; algorithm presentation and description of a simple application based on TTS and STT technologies. In summary, the results of the application testing are presented and requests for future development are indicated.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of an Embedded System for E-Waste Recognition
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis of an embedded e-waste recognition system, with the goal of evaluating its effectiveness and efficiency. The system under consideration uses advanced computer vision and machine learning techniques, making it an inferential alternative for solving the pressing e-waste problem. Key performance metrics including accuracy, latency, memory usage, and power consumption are evaluated. These metrics are essential for evaluating the practical feasibility of the embedded system in real applications.We present a custom software tool developed to visualize and record the images and classification results generated by the embedded system in real-time. This tool allows a detailed and in-depth investigation of the system's performance, enabling us to obtain valuable information about its efficiency. The analysis of the obtained results gives an objective insight into the strengths and weaknesses of the embedded system. Recommendations for potential improvements and optimizations are derived.The findings presented in this paper contribute to ongoing efforts to develop effective and reliable e-waste recognition solutions. This supports sustainable waste management and environmental protection.

articleTitle: Teaching Analogue Electronics through Simulations Using Performance-Centered Approach in Vocational Education and Training
abstract: This paper discusses the significance of performance-centered approach in teaching analogue electronics through simulations in vocational education and training. The course structure and the objectives are described. 21 video lessons with total duration more than 90 minutes are developed to support students in Computer modelling and simulation in Analogue Electronics (CMSAE) course in tasks performance. The preliminary results from the pilot phase of CMSAE indicate positive feedback from students, highlighting the course's relevance, structure, and applicability to the labor market's skill needs.

articleTitle: IMU Sensor Fusion with Quaternion Interval-Based Orientation Filters Processed over Smartphone Scanned Data
abstract: Quaternion-based and Interval-based methods are suitable solutions to be implemented as dedicated filters for IMU’s (Inertial Measurement Unit) sensor fusion. Usually, both solutions are not implemented together, because of the loss of performance. This article introduces and makes the first step on implementation of an effective solution, combining the advantages of Quaternion arithmetic (for rotation) and Interval arithmetic (for elimination of outliers), with improved hardware performance. The proposed approach is suitable for implementation over of reconfigurable FPGA target devices with flexible architecture, so that we could achieve precise orientation in real-time system using low-cost IMUs. Also, such a structure could allow a simple cost-free redesign and easy functional upgrade. Here, the proposed algorithm and the results of Quaternion arithmetic, based on data from built-in mobile phone’s IMU, are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: Inventory and Safety Stock Optimization
abstract: This research aims to develop a formal optimization problem that integrates estimates for supply management and reserve stock parameters. The latter is necessary to handle the production process with stochastic demands on the content of raw materials in the inventory. The problem being defined has both types of variables: the level of resource provision and the value of reserve stock. The optimization problem is compounded by simultaneous inventory of a set of materials. The problem is solved with data related to the preparation of livestock feed for growing pigs. A sensitivity analysis of the solutions to the problem is performed and analyzed.

articleTitle: Using an IoT system for monitoring climatic conditions during flowering in fruit plantations
abstract: The aim of this research is to use an IoT multi-sensor monitoring system, to track the temperature and relative humidity of the air, as well as the temperature in the active root-inhabiting soil layer during the flowering period of trees in an orchard, as an important stage of spring phenology. With the help of the system, there were detected negative temperatures at night and in early morning combined with high relative air humidity for a long time period, which in the monitored period can affect the coming harvest.

Author Keywords: air and soil temperature and moisture measurements

articleTitle: Neuromorphic Neurons and Networks for Artificial Intelligence Built Using Temporal Space Calculations
abstract: We deigned a spiking neural network that computes network weights in the temporal dimension. Such a network can be used for artificial intelligence and deep learning. We demonstrate circuits implementing blocks for building such a network and then a training model. This enables creation of efficient Hessenstein-Reichardt detectors observed in motion detection networks in the nature. The proposed network allows reconfiguration across network layers algorithmically.

articleTitle: Air parameters monitoring in urban area based on LoRaWAN: Data collection for environmental assessment
abstract: Advances in Internet of Things (IoT) technologies have given a strong progress in environmental monitoring, particularly in air quality assessment. Various technologies are being considered to realize IoT devices, of which LoRaWAN is one of the most promising. This paper presents a prototype of LoRaWAN End device for real-time environmental assessment that stores the measured data in the cloud. The user interface consists of a mobile application that connects to the cloud server to retrieve data and set connection settings.

articleTitle: A Fast Transient Response Capacitorless LDO Designed in 22FDX® Technology
abstract: This paper presents a low-dropout capacitorless linear regulator using a low output resistance buffer, designed in GlobalFoundries 22nm fully depleted silicon on insulator technology. The proposed LDO consumes 85 µA from 1.8 V power supply. The output voltage is configurable in the range of 0.9–1.25 V. The target maximum output current is 30 mA. The load transient response time is about 15 ns. The target is to have at least 20 dB Power Supply Rejection Ratio (PSRR) at 5 MHz (the frequency that the digital is operating on). The compact design is occupying area of only 0.18 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Embedded System for E-Waste Recognition Using Computer Vision
abstract: In this article we will showcase a novel embedded system for e-waste recognition. We will cover the hardware and software requirements of the system, as well as our methods for data acquisition, data processing, and model training and testing. System parameters, such as accuracy and power consumption, will be thoroughly analyzed in our next article.

articleTitle: State of health estimation of Lithium-ion batteries: A review of data-driven methods
abstract: This paper presents a systematic review of data-driven methods for state of health estimation of lithium-ion batteries. The growing interest in these methods is due to their capability to retrieve nonlinear relationships between data. Future research directions are presented to improve the accuracy and stability of machine learning methods for state of health estimation.

articleTitle: Radiationless energy calibration of radiation survey meters
abstract: Nnuclear spectrometers and/or dosemeters using photodetectors is proposed and investigated. Visible light pulses with different intensity and duration are used for irradiation of the detector instead of nuclear radiation sources. The calibration procedure is described in detail. Experimental results with a dosemeter for aerospace applications are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Application of Fuzzy Logic for Detection of Financial-Customs Violations
abstract: This paper proposes the application of Fuzzy Logic as a tool to detect customs and financial violations. The fuzzy rules are developed by the method of multi-subject multicriteria expertise. Synthetic data generated using Gretel online environment is used for testing. The resulting fuzzy rule system was tested with real data from the Customs Agency, and the results obtained showed very high accuracy.

articleTitle: Autonomous Street Lighting System with Batteries and PV Generators: System Modeling and Results
abstract: This study presents an autonomous street lighting system powered by batteries and PV generators. The feasibility study examines the advantages of off-grid operation, utilizing solar energy for sustainability. The experimental setup features a Victron BlueSolar 100/15 charge controller, JA Solar 420Wp PV module, and LED fixtures. PVSyst software models the system, determining optimal battery storage capacity based on predefined load profiles. Results highlight the system's efficiency and adaptability, providing insights for real-world implementation.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of a Phase-Shift Controlled LLC Resonant Converter
abstract: This paper performs a simulation study of the operation of a phase-shift controlled LLC resonant converter at frequencies above the resonant frequency. The circuit's performances at different phase-shift angles, loads and ratios between parallel and series inductances are analyzed. The output characteristics obtained from the simulations and their comparison with the theoretical results are discussed. The influence of different parameters on the output power regulation conditions while maintaining the ZVS conditions of the transistors in the "lagging" leg is analyzed. Simulations for continuous current mode have been implemented using OrCad PSpice. Good agreement between theoretical and simulation results is observed.

articleTitle: Application of Open-Source Software in Digital Electronics Education
abstract: The aim of the paper is to study the applicability of several open-source software products in digital electronics education. Specific examples of typical digital circuits are presented. Examples are presented using open-source software for synthesizing logic circuits, testing digital blocks implemented in VHDL. Simulation studies are presented, through which it is easier for students to understand the reasons for incorrect operation of a logic circuit when a malfunction is present.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of an LLC Resonant DC-DC Converter at Boost Mode
abstract: The subject of the present study is an LLC DC-DC converter operating in boost mode. An assumption is made that the circuit consists of ideal elements. The possible conditions for ZVS operation are discussed. Expressions are presented for the discontinuous current modes to model the processes in the resonant tank. Boundary conditions between the operating modes are also defined.

articleTitle: Development of a Laboratory System for the Study of Discrete-Circuit Basic LC Oscillators
abstract: This work presents the structure and the principle of operation of a laboratory system intended for laboratory practice in the course of Analog circuitry. The developed laboratory system has functional capabilities for experimental testing of two oscillator circuits generating sine waves, namely the LC oscillator with transformer-based positive feedback (Meissner oscillator) and the Colpitts oscillator. The study of the circuits initially started with testing of the selective LC amplifier for the Meissner circuit and a study of the LC frequency-selective network for the Colpitts configuration. The positive-feedback loop consisting of an amplifier and а frequency-selective network is then investigated at different operating points of the used transistors and various passive components in the positive feedback. In this way, the student's knowledge acquired on the basis of the lectures, as well as the acquisition of new practical skills, are strengthened. The developed laboratory system is intended for use by second-year students in the Bachelor's degree programs in "Electronic Information Systems" and "Automotive Electronics" at the Technical University of Sofia. Also, the system can be used for laboratory work in the course "Electronic Modules and Systems – Analog and Digital" studied by third-year students in the Bachelor's degree program of "Aeronautical Engineering"

articleTitle: Optimization of Heat Sink Design by Simulated Annealing Method
abstract: This work applies the Simulated Annealing method for multiobjective optimization of aluminum planar heat sink design. Two objective functions are considered independently and combined, first is temperature minimization at the base plate and second is the heat sink volume reduction. A Finite Element Method (FEM) is used to model the thermal field of the design variations under consideration. The optimization FEM model is built using FEMM software, applied via Octave-FEMM interface to Simulated Annealing toolbox in MatLab. Results are showing new capabilities for optimal heat sinks designs with reduced weight and improved heath conduction.

articleTitle: New Study Program in Space Systems and Communications Engineering
abstract: The paper presents an international project for competence building in higher education SPACECOM. It is an Erasmus+ co-funded project aimed to provide Uzbek universities with pilot Master's degree programmes in the field of space technologies. Its focus is also on development of competences and skills of young faculty members for innovative teaching in close cooperation with European universities, proved not only extremely relevant to meet the national needs and constraints, but being also a winning strategy for the improvement of higher education systems.

articleTitle: Influence of the Parasitic Components in Induction Motor
abstract: In the present paper, a simulation study of the influence of the parasitic components in a three-phase induction motor drive is made. A model including a three-phase uncontrollable rectifier, an inverter, a long cable and an induction motor was implemented. The model is described with mathematical equations and is implemented in PSIM software. In order to reduce the harmful effects of the long cable at high operating frequencies, a filter has been added. A comparison is made between the two models and a discussion is made in which the advantages and disadvantages of the proposed schemes are presented.

articleTitle: Piezo Effect of Polyvinylidene Fluoride Layer with Rochelle Salt
abstract: A piezo layer from polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) mixed with Rochelle salt(RS) was deposited for future electronics applications. The layers were obtained by solvent/antisolvent electrophoretic deposition. They are inhomogeneous and uneven composed of fibers and agglomerates of RS/PVDF mixture, individual PVDF fibers about 100 nm thick and RS crystals. Although inhomogeneous, the layers show an order of magnitude higher piezo modulus (413 pC/N) and comparable to inorganic piezo ceramics. Тhey can be used for energy harvesting systems and autonomous power supplies due to the high piezo effect and flexibility.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Designing Amplitude-Correction Sections Using an Active Implementation with an Operational Amplifier
abstract: The paper briefly presents the basic principles of amplitude correction. A model of an amplitude corrector using an active implementation with an op-amp is proposed. A methodology for its design is given in the paper. Program modules in MATLAB for the synthesis and analysis of amplitude correctors are created. Micro-Cap and Multisim simulations of the amplitude-corrector sections designed using the suggested methodology are given in the paper. Also, a laboratory board developed at the University of Ruse for the study of amplitude correctors and used in the educational process in the discipline "Communication Circuits" is presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Control of N87 Mn-Zn Ferrite Permeability Using Externally Applied Static Magnetic Field
abstract: This paper reports measurement results of N87 Mn-Zn ferrite's permeability response to externally applied static magnetic field. The measurements were conducted by applying magnetic field of a permanent magnet to a test magnetic component during usual ac excitation. Frequency dependencies of the complex initial permeability and respective loss tangent, as well as large signal square wave excited BH loops at single frequency, were taken under various configurations of the positioning between the magnet, the core under test and the excitation winding. The obtained results demonstrate strong dependency of both the real and imaginary parts of the initial permeability. At high frequencies the loss tangent gets lower. Control of the ferrite complex permeability and the usable frequency range of ferrites is achievable by variation of the strength of the external static magnetic field.

articleTitle: Combined footprint of solder paste - influence of bismuth content on solder strength
abstract: The article describes the mixing of two solder pastes in a combined footprint - standard SAC305 and low temperature 58Bi42Sn. The combined footprint was carried out with a jet printer. The experiments were performed with a different ratio between standard and low temperature pastes. It was measured whether changing the amount of bismuth in the solder paste changed the breaking strength of the solders. A large number of electronic components are examined and analyzed to obtain an objective statistical analysis.

articleTitle: A Server Application for Bridging the TCP/IP and Bluetooth Protocols
abstract: The following paper discusses the implementation of a software application meant to fill the gap between the Bluetooth and the TCP/IP protocol. This would allow to expand the wide area network Internet further by introducing new types of devices that currently exist in small local networks – battery-powered embedded devices. The application aims to make a protocol translation.

articleTitle: Hardware and software of a 3D printed humanoid hand
abstract: Creating low-cost and completely functional humanoid hand that meets individual needs and applications in prosthetics or robotics is still a challenge. This paper presents the development of an innovative 3D printed humanoid hand with modular fingers. This approach makes it possible to reduce the cost by taking advantage of the creation of complex shapes and individual sizes of the fingers. The software and hardware implementation of the modules is described. A control system has been designed that allows adjustment and control of the positions of fingers of different sizes and joint constraints. A 3D printed prototype is created. The hardware and software are tested. Main functional capabilities of the hand are studied.

articleTitle: FPGA-Based Implementation for QRS Detection in Electrocardiogram
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of a QRS detection algorithm in C with custom IP library blocks written in Verilog for a FPGA chip. The hardware design adds support for the processing of the data array that contains the electrocardiographic samples. Focus is put on the software and hardware structure, as well as some performance metrics – the used memory and the time for execution of the processing procedures. Final results shown that the hardware implementation is slower than the microprocessor-only implementation, its ROM usage is 700 bytes less. The RAM usage is equal in both cases. The hardware IP would also allow for other devices in the system to get more microprocessor time (e.g. interrupt handling).

articleTitle: Methodology for Determining the Thermal Properties of the Heat Insulation Panels Using a Gray Box Model
abstract: The main methodological steps in determining the coefficient of thermal conductivity of the tested thermal insulation panel are considered. An RC analogy to electrical circuits is defined where heat flow can be modeled as current, temperature as a voltage source, and thermal storage as capacitance. The developed methodology can also be used in the training of students in the field of measuring the properties of thermal insulation materials

articleTitle: Neuromorphic Assisted Sensor Grids
abstract: A particular problem in using artificial intelligence techniques in the sensor grid is the high power consumption. Remote sensors are usually limited by the amount of power available, thus our general goal is to minimize it while preserving accurate experimentation results. Using emerging technologies like spiking neural networks and neuromorphic hardware, we can create sensor grids that perform data processing with preserving low power consumption. In this paper, we demonstrate a remote node with integrated visual sensor that works on less than 10mW of energy, while performing continuous scene monitoring, object detection and classification. The system has intelligent power management and the ability to send data wirelessly.

articleTitle: Multichannel Non-Contact System for Breathing Detection and Respiratory Rate Measurement Using Capacitive Electrodes
abstract: The breathing and respiratory rate are one of the important parameters in vital signs monitoring systems. There are various types of methods and sensors used for biomedical and vital signs parameters measurements. Non-invasive and non-contact of them are preferred due to the patient comfort, but they require a new methods and processing algorithms due to high noises level or another reasons. In this work we present a breathing detect and respiratory rate calculating algorithm for the monitoring system based on the microcontroller with CTMU and sheet with a matrix of capacitive electrodes.

articleTitle: Two Approaches in Designing the Learning Content and Measurement of Achievements – European Credit System for Vocational Education and Training and Micro-Credentials
abstract: The paper explores the advantages of two European-wide approaches in learning content design and evaluation of achievements- European credit system for vocational education and training (ECVET) and Micro-credentials. The tendencies in more dynamic content design in smaller learning units is also explored. The examples of learning materials design, incorporated in Learning management systems (LMS) developed by a team leaded by the author is presented.

articleTitle: A Review of Industry Quality Improvement Strategies through DoE Statistical Techniques
abstract: The use of statistical techniques has become a key tool for optimizing quality, productivity and cost control in the production of products or the development of services in industry. For this reason, this article discusses the procedures, phases and activities enshrined in the concepts of Six Sigma, DFSS (Design for Six Sigma) and Taguchi Methods for solving quality problems in various industrial fields and improving the business through the application of statistical tools for DoE (Design of Experiment).

articleTitle: SPICE modeling of the Li-ion battery pack’s charge behavior using QUCS-S software
abstract: The paper studies SPICE modeling of a Li-ion battery pack, specifically its charge behavior. For modeling the nonlinear relationship between current and voltage during charge, a method suitable for implementation in the QUCS-S open-source software environment is proposed. Real measured data from the charge process of standard Li-ion batteries with automotive application were used for the modeling. Through software processing of these data, the parameters necessary for the creation of the models were extracted. Model verification results are presented.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Control Algorithms for a Power converter - Switched Reluctance Motor System in Motoring Mode
abstract: This paper presents a simulation study and comparative analysis of control algorithms using a unipolar modulation of a converter-switched reluctance motor system in motoring mode. The analysis is performed based on power losses in the converter and motor efficiency and torque ripples. The study has been performed by examining the power losses in the converter and motor, efficiency and torque ripples in MATLAB/Simulink environment for each of the selected algorithms while varying different input parameters. Based on the obtained results, recommendations and basic considerations are formulated to select the most suitable control algorithm for the system operation in the motoring mode.

articleTitle: Hybrid Solar Inverters evaluation
abstract: Achieving full utilization of the solar resource inevitably requires storage of excess energy during peak generation. Adding a battery to a solar inverter makes it a hybrid one. These inverters are the main steppingstone in achieving the goal of EU for decarbonization by full utilization of renewable resources. However, in order to achieve this goal their efficiency must be as high as possible during battery charging or discharging. This depends mainly on the power topology that is used. The paper presents the power topologies used in market available hybrid inverters alongside measured efficiencies during operation. Based on these data a novel power topology is presented that increased the efficiency in certain scenarios. Experimental verification of the topology during battery charging is presented to show the advantages.

articleTitle: Dual Active Bridge Resonant Converter with Variable Frequency Control
abstract: A dual active bridge series resonant converter operating above its resonant frequency is investigated. A control method with a frequency variation in different ranges is used. As a result, the dependencies of the RMS inductor current from the output voltage are built. The experiment with a 200 W model of the converter validated the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Moodle Based Learning Management System (LMS) Platform for Microelectronics Education
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of an online platform for e-learning in the field of microelectronics using the Moodle learning management system (LMS). The paper discusses the theoretical background of Moodle as an open-source LMS, its features and functionalities, and its suitability for delivering e-learning experiences. Additionally, it highlights the importance of e-learning in microelectronics, outlining the challenges and benefits associated with this approach. A real developed courses for microelectronics are presented.

articleTitle: Method for cooling lithium-ion batteries in electric bicycles
abstract: A method for air cooling of lithium-ion batteries in electric bicycles, motorcycles, scooters, and other electrically powered vehicles is presented. The developed method does not require additional power supply and utilizes the airflow generated during the vehicle's movement. This airflow is separated from the air stream that cools the battery pack, enabling the cooling system to operate under various weather conditions. The developed design is robust, cost-effective, resistant to vibrations, shock loads and contamination.

articleTitle: Real-time online measurement of automotive pollution emissions
abstract: The vehicle pollution emissions are one of the most pressing issues of the cities. The new electric cars are still a source of pollution such as particulate matters while the gasoline and the diesel engines emit CO/HC/NOx and fine particles. The real driving emission control is sometimes very expensive and not applicable while the laboratory testing shows incorrect results e.g. 50% direct injection vehicles without gasoline particle filter fail RDE test. Therefore a smart emission measuring systems should be implemented to obtain the real-driving vehicle emissions, which is capable for real-time remote monitoring via Internet connection.

articleTitle: Synthesis, Analysis and Implementation of Partial Counters Using Integrated Circuits
abstract: The paper presents the processes of synthesis, analysis, and implementation of counters and frequency dividers using integrated circuits from the 74xx library. All the synthesized circuits are built and tested in Logisim. The work is related to the Teamwork Project in the course "Digital Circuits" for students-bachelors of the "Computer Systems and Technologies" specialty at the University of Ruse.

articleTitle: Intuitive Approach to Active Digital Filter Design. Part II: Principle of Higher-order Low-pass Filters
abstract: In digital signal processing (DSP), digital filtering is a crucial signal processing task used to remove unwanted frequencies and noise, enhance signal quality, and increase the signal-to-noise ratio of processed signals. In Part I, the principle of integrator-based closed-loop filters, namely active digital filters, was described in detail with examples of first-order low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, and band-rejection filters. The approach is based on feedback control theory and uses digital integrators to build stable negative feedback digital signal processing systems. This paper continues to reveal the design of second and higher-order active low-pass filters and demonstrates how easy it is to implement various filtering functions such as Bessel, Butterworth, and Chebyshev in closed-loop architectures. The frequency characteristics of the presented filters fully overlap with their analog Sallen-Key equivalents. Finally, an application of active digital filters for ECG processing is disclosed.

articleTitle: PIC MCU to FPGA Data Transffer Optimization Over Parallel-Master-Port
abstract: Two approaches are used in programmable devices – the use of MCU or FPGA. MCU facilitates the transfer of existing solutions between different MPU platforms while FPGA facilitates the parallelism of processes and connectivity. In this way, these two approaches should not be opposed, but must be used complementary and this process is in progress now. The article looks at the issue of scheme and program optimization of bidirectional data exchange between PIC MCU and FPGA.

articleTitle: Design of temperature-independent reference voltage source
abstract: The article focuses on the design of analog integrated circuits with specific temperature requirements for their parameters. It presents the design of a temperature-independent reference voltage source using MOS transistors in weak inversion within 45nm technology. The design is performed by two methodologies – a conventional one utilizing the equations of the model based on the threshold voltage, as well as the gm/ID methodology.

articleTitle: Novel Linear Step-up Power Supply Module for Detector Systems
abstract: A circuit solution for a linear DC to DC step-up converter suitable for powering detector systems which have high sensitivity to noise is described. The proposed method uses several optocouplers based on photovoltaics. Experimental results and an aerospace application are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Improving the print quality of a budget 3D FDM printer by replacing the factory-installed stepper motor drivers
abstract: This paper describes optimizing the performance of a low-cost FDM 3D printer by replacing the factory driver circuits for the printer's stepper motors with ones that allow finer microstepping operation. It also describes the software tuning process of the 3D printer's Marlin firmware after the driver circuits have been changed using the Pronterface software program. Results confirming the improved 3D printer performance and print quality are shown after 3D printing the same test part with the same slicer program settings before and after the driver circuitry replacement.

articleTitle: Derivation of numerical criteria for the occurrence of natural phenomena in video sequences
abstract: In this paper are presented the results from an analysis of the information, obtained from dataset of one year video records. The results show that some natural phenomena could be detected by simple numerical criteria. The records have been taken by outdoor surveillance cameras. The applied data processing aims to determine criteria for the occurrence of events affecting the visibility in images. The technique uses dark channel prior images (DCPI) and correlated color temperature (CCT) for limited areas located at identical positions within consecutive frames.

articleTitle: Utilization of Infrared Thermography for Battery Performance Inspection
abstract: The paper analyzes the approach and key considerations in using infrared thermography to remotely identify key internal characteristics of batteries. The experimental results of the study, which concerns two different types of batteries - lead-acid and lithium-ion (designated as "good" and "bad", according to certain criteria), promises the possibility for implementing automated remote diagnostics in real-world operating conditions, allowing for the evaluation of battery performance and preemptive determination of the type of potential defect that has occurred.

articleTitle: Simulation and Laboratory Study of Voltage Multipliers in the Course Power Supply
abstract: In the concept of the "Industry 5.0" standard, emphasis is placed on the human factor and the person as the center of the production process. This necessitates the implementation of synergistic models, as an integral component of the successful educational process, to combine theoretical, practical, and scientific-research competencies in future engineers. The purpose of this paper is to present an approach to the study of voltage multipliers in the "Power Supply" course of the "Electronics" major at the University of Ruse "Angel Kanchev". Students first design the multiplication schemes, simulate and practically investigate a developed laboratory model, thereby consolidating their theoretical and practical knowledge and competencies.

articleTitle: Switch-Time neurons. Definition and types
abstract: Neural networks are used in forecasting or predicting given output variable based on information provided by a set of input variables. There are also other types of models used for the same purpose: linear regression models, non-linear regression-based models, polynomial approximation etc.While linear and non-linear regression models are parametric models, neural networks, like polynomial approximation models, are semi-parametric. Neural networks models, in contrast with polynomial semi-parametric models, don’t provide closed-form solution, so only approximate solution can be provided by the neural networks.In this article, we consider the Switch-time neuron based on the so called Switch-time (ST) distribution [4]. More specifically, we consider two types of Switch-time neurons: one-side Switch-time neuron (ST neuron) and double-side Switch-time neuron (DST neuron) and present R code for simulating different examples of both types of neurons.As the concept neuron is close to the concept regression, we may by analogy consider Switch-time (stopit) regression [5] of both types.

articleTitle: Infrared temperature measurement of wall areas with automatic distance correction
abstract: Infrared temperature measurement of wall areas with automatic distance correction is a technique used to accurately determine the temperature on specific sections of a wall. The process involves using infrared technology to identify thermal patterns emitted by the surface, allowing for non-contact and rapid measurements. The automatic distance correction ensures precise readings by compensating for variations in target distance. This method proves useful in a variety of applications, such as insulation evaluations, energy efficiency assessments, and thermal analysis of building structures.

articleTitle: Research of Sequential Algorithms for Graph Model Decomposition
abstract: The subject of this paper is sequential decomposition algorithms. They are applied to graph models of various sizes. A study of their speed and applicability was made with software applications developed for the purpose. The obtained results are presented in tabular and graphical form. Conclusions have been made about their applicability in the design automation of circuit and systems.

articleTitle: Sensorless Determination of the Temperature and Solar Radiation of a Photovoltaic Module
abstract: This paper proposes a sensorless determination of the temperature and solar radiation of photovoltaic module. Expressions of the main characteristics and parameters that must be considered when modeling a photovoltaic module have been obtained. Results are presented to illustrate the accuracy of the proposed methodology, compared to an industrial measurement device.

articleTitle: Sustainability Validation of a LabVIEW Based System for Biomarkers Detection
abstract: In this paper, the suitability of a biomarker detection method is investigated and verified. The method consists in determining the frequency change of the intersection point of the frequency responses of two microcantilevers. A special experimental setup was created to investigate the vibrations of two microcantilevers. LabVIEW software was created to control the experiment and to receive and process the experimental data. The main theoretical relations on which the method is based are derived. The experimental results obtained on the one hand confirm the theory and on the other hand verify the suitability of the method.

articleTitle: Approach of Successive Suppression of Mains Interference and Baseline Drift in ECG Signals
abstract: The article presents an approach for the simultaneous removal of baseline drift and mains interference from ECG signals. The approach is based on a pipelined implementation of an adaptive rejection filter for the mains frequency and a high-pass filter to remove the baseline drift. A program procedure is proposed that adapts the rejection filter to the deviation in the mains frequency. A program has been compiled that determines the parameters of the high-pass filter depending on the set cut-off frequency for the high-pass filtering. Tests conducted with artificial and real ECG signals and interferences show very good baseline drift removal and completely suppress mains interferences with minimal impact on the ECG signal shape.

articleTitle: A Secure Firmware Update over the Air of ESP32 using MQTT Protocol from Cloud
abstract: In this paper are made an scientifically applied experiment that update controlling firmware of an IoT embedded system. This are achieved by using the MQTT protocol and encrypting the connection between the IoT Device and the IoT Cloud. TLS SSL certificates were used to encrypt the data through the MQTT protocol.

articleTitle: Improvements and Shortcomings in The First Stage of Scrum Implementation in Medium-Sized IT Companies
abstract: The application of the SCRUM procedure in hardware projects is of great importance because the material costs and the high risk of irreversible costs caused by changes negatively affect the business of IT companies that produce hardware. After the implementation of the pilot project in the software company, the introduction of agile methods was started in medium-sized companies that produce electronic equipment. General improvements and current problems that occur in the first stages of the implementation of agile method and scrum framework in a medium-sized IT company are presented in this paper. In order to see the workload of the team, Velocity Chart of the amount of work done after each spring was used. The team's work is shown on the Sprint Burndown Chart.

articleTitle: A Research on High Efficiency InnoSwitch3-EP GaN AC/DC Integrated Circuit
abstract: In this paper, application and research issues related to novel quasi-resonant AC/DC integrated circuit with GaN transistors are discussed. The results of the design and investigation of a laptop power supply device with an output power of 65W implemented with INN3679C-H60X of the InnoSwitch3-EP family are presented. The performance oscillograms of the GaN power transistor as well as the input, output and regulation characteristics of the power supply are presented.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Estimation of Battery Cell Age
abstract: Assessing battery health has been a topic in many modern scientific works due to the industrial push towards more sustainable electronic systems. In order for the processing of State-of-Health evaluation to be performed in an automated manner - Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning algorithmic methods have become the dominant models used for regression and classification tasks. Within this work we have developed and presented a Deep Neural Network battery age classifier, analyzing a set of parameters which are the curve approximating coefficients for the processes of charging and discharging of Li-Ion cells.

articleTitle: Laboratory Setup for Studying Heat Transfer through Thermal Insulation Panels
abstract: The climatic conditions change, the depletion of the earth's energy resources, the greenhouse effect, and the need to reduce carbon dioxide emissions in the atmosphere are the strongest arguments that require adequate training of the students in universities in the direction of achieving new energy policies. This necessitates introducing and implementing new approaches and principles for collection, analyzes and presentation of measurement data on certain processes or phenomena through the use of laboratory models for training. Modern technologies provide opportunities for the application and search of new teaching methods in universities, which leads to adaptation and a change of thinking, for both teachers and students.

articleTitle: ICT for Integrating the Project-Based Learning Method in Bulgarian Education
abstract: The introduction of information and communication technologies in education is transforming the way of teaching, learning and managing the educational process. This has been particularly noticeable over the past two decades, seeing not only the digitalization of the educational process, but also the emergence of new teaching and learning methods and approaches. These methods serve as a link between the traditional and the innovative, between the goals and results of modern education. In this paper, ICT for integrating project-based learning as a method linking traditions with innovation and technology in education are explored. An experiment was conducted with three groups of students who were trained by traditional and project-based methods during their full-time studies. At the end of the experiment, students were evaluated against the teaching method. The results show a better success of the group with project-based learning, which confirms the main advantages of the method for achieving the goals of 21st century education.

articleTitle: A Web-based Antenna Positioning System with Application in Radio Astronomy
abstract: In this paper is presented a web-based antenna positioning system with application in radio astronomy. It is intended for long-term Sun tracking in order to register electromagnetic emissions with wavelengths in meter range. The proposed system is based on feedback concept in terms of minimizing the error between target and measured azimuth and elevation angles. The system has been tested and the achieved accuracy for azimuth and elevation angles is better than 1.0°, which is fully acceptable considering the directivity of the used antenna.

articleTitle: Compliance and Data Security in Document Management Systems
abstract: This paper discusses the critical aspects of compliance and data security in document management systems (DMS). The importance of adhering to regulatory requirements and implementing robust security measures to protect sensitive information is discussed. Compliance with regulatory standards and data encryption are highlighted. The importance of access control, user permissions, audit trails, activity logs, version control and document history in the context of document management are explained. The role of secure storage and backup, as well as data retention for robust DMS implementation are mentioned.

articleTitle: Tolerance Analysis of a Resonant DC/AC Converter with Reverse Diodes Operating at Control Frequency Below and Above Resonance
abstract: The manuscript presents a tolerance analysis of a transistor series resonant inverter with reverse diodes based on the use of a model and mathematical software. Continuous - continuous current mode operation at below and above resonant control frequency is considered. By applying an author's program, a 20% change in the values of the resonance elements was set and visualized. In this way, the wobble of the tolerances on working loads of two specially designed for the purpose of the study case of transistor series resonant inverters has been investigated. 3-D characteristics of the source variables are obtained, which give the range of variation of the current and voltage loading of the power circuit.

articleTitle: Pipeline-accurate Instruction Cycle Measurements for Microprocessor Model Extraction
abstract: The following paper presents a measurement method for extracting the number of cycles used by the microprocessor instructions of a 16-bit microarchitecture. The purpose of these measurements is to create a lookup table containing cycle costs for each instruction and for each pipeline stage. This information is needed to create a cycle-accurate microprocessor model.

articleTitle: Use of Software Simulators in Digital Logic Design Education
abstract: This paper presents the use of software simulators throughout the whole digital logic design learning process. Specific examples of the application of these software products in the lecture material, the laboratory exercises, the course project in the discipline, and exam preparation are given. Free simulators are used, and of course, there are also paid ones. The use of such programs enhances student learning.

articleTitle: Data Transmission between IoT Modules using Audio Steganography
abstract: Data in sensor networks, transmitted usually between IoT modules, should be protected from unauthorized access to prevent erroneous actions with fatal consequences. Methods should be applied to encode or hide the transmitted data. This paper proposes to apply audio steganography methods to hide the data. An algorithm and program modules have been developed. The main experimental results demonstrating the correct and reliable hiding of data transmitted between IoT modules are briefly presented applying the proposed algorithm based on steganography.

articleTitle: Use of Infrared Radiometry for Livestock Temperature Measurements
abstract: The research aims to calculate and visualize the appropriate maximum distances for precision cattle thermographic measurements. Factors relevant to radiometric temperature studies are investigated and conclusions are drawn about their influence. The results show that the maximum recommended distance for performing a precise radiometric temperature measurement of an individual cattle with a handheld thermal camera is about 3 m.

articleTitle: Application and Performance Analysis of LoRa End Devices for Monitoring of Indoor Lighting Systems
abstract: This paper examines the implementation of an energy-efficient narrowband long-range (LoRa) communication network in the Internet of Things (IoT) concept for management and monitoring of indoor lighting systems. For this purpose, three variants of LoRa end devices configured at frequency 868 MHz and Spreading Factor (SF 9), used in particular for an indoor lighting system monitoring, were developed, tested and compared. The obtained results include determining the maximum network range (communication distance), packet delivery time and RSSI signal level.

articleTitle: Analysis of Current, Polarization and Lithium Concentration in the Porous Electrode of a Lithium-ion Battery during High-frequency, High-current (10,000C) Flow
abstract: Using an equivalent circuit model of the porous electrodes of the positive and negative electrodes that takes into account diffusion in the pores, we analyzed the current, polarization, and lithium concentration in the porous electrodes of a lithium ion battery when a high current sine wave corresponding to 10000C passes through one cycle. As a result, at high frequency currents above 10 kHz, the Faraday current in the electrode is small and the charging current in the electric double layer is large, while at 100 kHz, both polarization and lithium concentration changes are small. From this result, it is expected that the application of AC current at 100 kHz has little effect on the electrode.

articleTitle: Large Signal Complex Permeability for Design and Simulation of Power Electronics Circuits
abstract: This paper introduces a concept for a Large Signal Complex Permeability (LSCP) magnetic cores characterization based on square wave excitation. The LSCP derivation is detailed through an exemplary measurement performed and its validity is verified through circuits’ simulations fed with experimental waveforms. With the LSCP data, the magnetizing inductance and power loss resistance resulting from the magnetic core in use can be more arcuately predicted in terms of the actual switching converter operating conditions.

articleTitle: Model-based Investigation of the Control Systems of the PMSM and Induction Motor for Application in EVs
abstract: This article presents the main features of two mathematical models of electric motors. The first model used two synchronous machines with permanent magnets coupled to each other. In the second model, a similar model including an induction machine and a synchronous machine with permanent magnets is implemented. The purpose of the realized models is to represent the principle of operation of an electric vehicle through a sufficiently close approximation. The models are implemented in the MATLAB/Simulink programming environment. Also, the main advantages and disadvantages in the way of controlling the different types of machines are presented, regarding their energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Sensor array current consumption optimizer with Gradient Descent
abstract: This article aims to show an example realization of Gradient descent algorithm for power supply consumption optimization in embedded sensor systems by means of adjusting measurement cycles to meet a given user target input. When execution is complete, the tool returns measurement cycle information that satisfy the given user target for overall current consumption. Example implementation is done in Python.

articleTitle: Implementing ownCloud for Scientific Project Coordination as Document Management System
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical background and implementation approach for utilizing ownCloud, an open-source cloud storage platform, as a document management system (DMS) for project reporting in an educational project. The document outlines the motivation for adopting ownCloud, discusses its key features and benefits and presents a step-by-step implementation process. The paper also highlights the potential impact of ownCloud as a secure and scalable solution for managing documents in project implementation, fostering collaboration, and enhancing data privacy.

articleTitle: Advancements in Main Battle Tank Simulations: Integrating Microcontrollers and Unreal Engine for Realistic Interior Panel Recreation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing main battle tank (MBT) training through the recreation of realistic interior panels. By utilizing microcontrollers and electronic components, a working control panel simulator is developed, allowing trainees to interact with the specific systems and controls of MBTs. The integration of Unreal Engine 4 as the simulation environment provides a highly realistic visual rendering and robust physics simulation capabilities, creating an immersive training experience. The study highlights the potential of combining hardware implementation and advanced simulation technologies in MBT training.

articleTitle: Provision and Assessment of Wireless Coverage and Communication Range of a LoRaWAN Network in an Urban Environment
abstract: LoRaWAN networks are becoming increasingly popular in building communication platforms for IoT applications. It is a narrowband communication that is actively used in the deployment of IoT and industrial IoT networks in smart applications and platforms for intelligent cities and factories. The attractiveness of this technology lies in the possibility of reliable data transmission at low speeds over long distances at extremely low signal power levels, including in highly noisy transmission environments. A key design point is the planning the optimal area to provide reliable radio coverage for narrowband data transmission in the network based on the specifics of the respective application. A simulation prediction and analysis of the radio coverage to determine its maximum range is considered. The results are compared with real measurements for the same radio coverage area in order to evaluate the data transmission efficiency and evaluate the quality of service.

articleTitle: Business Management by Portfolio Optimization Model
abstract: Business management must take into account the relationship between income and expenses incurred in the production of goods. The paper applies a quantitative approach to the assessment of production cost levels and their relationship to production revenue. The quantitative approach is based on the definition and solution of appropriate portfolio problem. It gives as an optimal solution the level of reduction or increase of relevant production costs by means of maximizing production income. The risk in such decisions is assessed on the basis of the formal definitions applied in the portfolio theory. This quantitative decision-making model is empirically tested with real data of animal husbandry. Numerical results show the advantages of the resulting portfolio model compared to the current business practice of animal husbandry.

articleTitle: Design of an embedded environment monitoring system with emphasis on low power consumption
abstract: The following paper explores the design of a battery-powered embedded environment monitoring system. It prioritizes low power consumption and accurate measurement parameters. Achieving this is made possible through the implementation of smart-wake-up signal thresholds, which are derived from correlating sensor measurements. By intelligently optimizing power usage and maintaining measurement accuracy, the proposed system offers a reliable and efficient solution for environmental monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Electronic Document Management Systems in the Context of Scientific and Educational Project Management. Comparative Study and Discussion
abstract: An examination of the role of document management systems in scientific project management was presented. Limitations of traditional approaches and the benefits of modern electronic and cloud-based systems are discussed. The paper emphasizes the importance of compliance and data security in document management and highlights the integration with other project management tools. Emerging trends in artificial intelligence and data analytics are also discussed.

articleTitle: Monitoring of living conditions in cow farm through a multisensory system
abstract: Monitoring of living conditions in Cow farm through a multisensory system. This study aims to trace factors from living conditions in cow farm using a multisensory monitoring system, to outline the importance and to show some benefits of using this type of systems. Based on the data obtained, a temperature-humidity index was calculated. The results show that the living conditions of cows for milk in the studied farm for this period are extreme in terms of heat stress. The multisensory environmental monitoring system provides adequate information about the living conditions of cows for milk.

articleTitle: Overview of methodologies for initial design of CMOS integrated circuits in deep submicron processes in different regions of inversion
abstract: This paper presents an overview and comparison of three popular methodologies used for initial sizing of analog CMOS circuits in deep submicron processes. The following methodologies are considered: design with models, based on the threshold voltage; design with simplified EKV models; design with the gm/ID methodology. The focus of the paper is on comparison of the accuracy of these methodologies when the design is performed in different regions of inversion of the transistor - weak, moderate and strong.

articleTitle: Methods for Automated PCB Testing - Requiarements, Rules and Implementation
abstract: For the verification of electronic devices, a test instruction is prepared with a specific strategy on what and how to test. The article discusses all the types of testing currently used to verify PCBs: bare board and assembled PCBs - where the functionality of the device is verified. An overview is given of the nature of each test, the sequence that is followed in the test, the equipment required for the purpose. An example is given of an assembly diagram of a device intended for series production, which has gone through all stages of design, testing and implementation, with special attention paid to the test points of the circuit board.

articleTitle: Design of the Blockchain System for the Generation and Verification of Diplomas
abstract: The creation of blockchain systems for generation and verification of diplomas would reduce the possibility of forgeries that may occur, as diplomas are important documents that characterize a person in a professional sense. Through the paper we will describe the importance of the application of blockchain systems in higher education institutions for the generation and verification of diplomas. The design of the smart contract will be made through UML diagrams, respectively class diagrams. We will elaborate some techniques for smart contract testing.

articleTitle: Intuitive Approach to Active Digital Filter Design. Part I: Principle of First-order Filters
abstract: Analog signals are usually digitized and further processed using various algorithms and procedures for digital data analysis. In digital signal processing (DSP), digital filtering is a crucial signal processing task that is used to enhance signal quality and increase the signal-to-noise ratio of a processed stream. This paper presents an original, intuitive, and easy-to-implement approach to the design of integrator-based closed-loop infinite-impulse-response filters, namely active digital filters. The approach is based on the feedback control theory and uses digital integrators to build stable negative feedback DSP systems that allow easy implementation of various filtering functions: low-pass, high-pass, etc. The filter cutoff frequency can be controlled using a single coefficient and adapted to the application needs. The presented active filters offer the simplest possible architecture and are well-suited for many DSP applications.

articleTitle: A specifics overview of Systems for monitoring security events in different areas
abstract: Monitoring systems are widespread in various areas. This software helps system administrators monitor the organization's infrastructure, and it can be enhanced using technologies such as the Internet of Things, Blockchain, and Artificial intelligence. These systems monitor sensors, traffic, and applications and alert in case of security incidents, malfunctions, or outages. This research presents an overview of the different fields where centralized monitoring systems could be used and the threats of cybersecurity attacks to them. Utilizing large groups of devices and sensors can lead to the compromise of some of them. Therefore, new methodologies and technologies must be developed to meet the requirements regarding security, reliability, and privacy of personal data. This paper will also briefly explore the different types of physical security systems used in buildings, their integration, and centralized monitoring.

articleTitle: Study of digital modulated signals, using PSPICE
abstract: PSPICE is a widely used computer program in teaching in the Faculties of Telecommunications and Electronics. The students master this program and handle it skillfully. This is the main reason for using this computer program when studying digitally modulated signals. In the presented work this program has been applied to the study of 16 QAM modulated signals. Also the impact of external interfering signal has been examined.

articleTitle: Bending Influence on the Flexible Interdigital Structures
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant increase in interest in the use of flexible sensor structures for various applications. These structures are relatively inexpensive and can be fabricated in different shapes and sizes. The present article investigates three types of flexible capacitive sensor structures with different forms. The influence of bending on their capacitance, impedance, and dielectric losses in the frequency domain has been studied. Some of the obtained results are presented graphically, and an analysis of the properties of the structures has been conducted.

articleTitle: Design of Power Supply Circuit for Measurements of Geomagnetically Induced Currents in Power Networks
abstract: In this paper is presented power supply circuit designed to deliver desire energy to magnetometers, used for measurements of geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) in a high voltage (HV) networks. The buck-boost dc-dc converter’s topology is investigated with software Cadence OrCAD. The input voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</inf> is expected to vary between 8 V and 15 V. The presented converter ensures stable dc output voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">out</inf> of 12 V. The power supply circuit is implemented on PCB. Efficiency as function of input voltage is investigated. The maximum achieved efficiency result of the designed circuit is equal to 85.7 %.

articleTitle: The Technological Ecosystem of Modern Wildfire Detection: A Review
abstract: Wildfire detection has been at the focal point of many research works in the past 20 years due to the non-material and material damages that they cause. Within this work we present an in-depth review of the modern technological ecosystem of wildfire early detection. Discussed have been wildfire propagation modeling, wildfire risk assessment, environmental contributing factors, forest fire emitted particulates. Presented were wireless sensor node systems, watchtower, satellite-based, unmanned aerial vehicle and narrow-band hyper-spectral methods for detecting wildfires.

articleTitle: Liability Associated with AI Systems under the Bulgarian Criminal Code: Requirements, Approaches and Proposals
abstract: The article aims to develop further the analysis on the criminal liability associated with AI entities under the Bulgarian Criminal law. The first part discusses the main concepts and requirements regarding the elaboration of regulation of criminal liability associated with the development, deployment, and use of AI systems. The second part offers some approaches and proposals for such regulation, accompanied by relevant examples. Finally, conclusions are drawn on the possibilities to adequately address the criminal liability associated with AI entities under the Bulgarian criminal law.

articleTitle: A Practical Computer Architecture Education with RISC-V and TL-Verilog
abstract: The report presents a hands-on learning approach that can be implemented in the Computer Architectures labs. A model of a pipelined microarchitecture RISC-V processor core developed using the high-level hardware description language TL-Verilog is described. Basic steps for implementation and visualization of the model are proposed. The necessity of its application in the educational process of students with different training profiles is substantiated.

articleTitle: Overview of the application of laser technologies in medicine and cosmetics
abstract: The development of laser technology in recent decades has led to a rethinking of many dogmas in the field of medicine and cosmetics. Practices that have been known for years are undergoing a significant change and pushing forward the development in these areas, bringing exceptional benefits to people and significantly supporting the work of medical professionals, as well as taking the cosmetic industry on a qualitatively new path.

articleTitle: The Impact of E-learning Techniques on Education Process. Platform Selection and Comparison
abstract: This paper explores the impact of e-learning educational process over the classical form. It examines the benefits and challenges of e-learning, ranging from increased accessibility and flexibility to personalized learning experiences. By analyzing various e-learning platforms, including Coursera, Udemy, Khan Academy and others, this study highlights their features, pricing models and engagement strategies. Based on this study a selection of suitable platforms for different sciences is proposed.
